items.stem: If the angle of depression of an object from a 75 m high tower is 30°, then the distance of the object from the tower is
items.answer: The tower AB = 75 m is the perpendicular and the object's distance OB from the foot is the base. The angle of depression at the top equals the angle of elevation at the object, so in the right triangle, tan30° = AB/OB. Then 1/√3 = 75/OB, so OB = 75√3 m.

items.stem: If the height and length of the shadow of a man are equal, then the angle of elevation of the sun is,
items.answer: Let AB be the man's height and BC his shadow, with AB = BC. In right triangle ABC, tanθ = AB/BC = AB/AB = 1, so tanθ = tan45° and θ = 45°.

items.stem: A tree casts a shadow 15 m long on the level of ground, when the angle of elevation of the sun is 45°. The height of a tree is
items.answer: Let BC be the tree and AB its shadow of 15 m, the right angle being at B. In triangle ABC, tan45° = BC/BA, so BC/15 = 1 and BC = 15 m. The tree is 15 m high.

items.stem: The ratio of the length of a rod and its shadow is 1 : √3 then the angle of elevation of the sun is
items.answer: Let the rod be AB = h and its shadow BC = √3 h, with θ the sun's elevation. In right triangle ABC, tanθ = h/(√3 h) = 1/√3, so θ = 30°.

items.stem: In the given figure, the positions of the observer and the object are mentioned, the angle of depression is
items.answer: The angle of depression is measured from the observer's horizontal ray down to the line of sight. That horizontal is parallel to the ground, so the angle of depression ∠XCA equals the alternate angle ∠CAB = 60° marked at the object. The angle of depression is 60°.

items.stem: A tree is broken by the wind. The top struck the ground at an angle of 30° and at distance of 10 m from its root. The whole height of the tree is (√3 = 1.732)
items.answer: Let CB be the part still standing and CD the broken part that fell, so the fallen piece AC = CD. In right triangle CDB, ∠CDB = 30° and DB = 10 m. From tan30° = CB/DB, CB = 10/√3; from cos30° = DB/DC, DC = 20/√3 = AC. The whole tree is AC + CB = 20/√3 + 10/√3 = 30/√3 = 10√3 m.

items.stem: A circle artist is climbing a 20 m long rope, which is tightly stretched and tied from the top of a vertical pole to the ground, then the height of pole, if the angle made by the rope with the ground level is 30°, is
items.answer: Let AB be the pole and CA the 20 m rope, meeting the ground at 30°. In right triangle ABC, sin30° = AB/AC, so 1/2 = AB/20 and AB = 10 m. The pole is 10 m high.

items.stem: The length of a string between a kite and a point on the ground is 85 m. If the string makes an angle θ with level ground such that tanθ = 15/8, then the height of kite is
items.answer: From tanθ = 15/8, cotθ = 8/15 and cosec²θ = 1 + 64/225 = 289/225, so cosecθ = 17/15 and sinθ = 15/17. With the string AB = 85 m as the hypotenuse, sinθ = BC/AB gives 15/17 = BC/85, so BC = 75 m. The kite is 75 m high.

items.stem: The top of two poles of height 20 m and 14 m are connected by a wire. If the wire makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal, then the length of the wire is
items.answer: Let CD = 20 m be the taller pole and AB = 14 m the shorter one, with BE drawn horizontal so that CE = AB = 14 m. Then DE = CD − CE = 20 − 14 = 6 m. In right triangle BDE, sin30° = DE/BD, so 1/2 = 6/BD and BD = 12 m. The wire is 12 m long.

items.stem: An observer, 1.5 m tall is 20.5 away from a tower 22 m high, then the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the eye of observer is
items.answer: Let BE = 22 m be the tower and AD = 1.5 m the observer, D being the eye, and draw DC parallel to AB. Then DC = AB = 20.5 m and EC = BE − BC = 22 − 1.5 = 20.5 m. In right triangle DCE, tanθ = CE/DC = 20.5/20.5 = 1, so θ = 45°.

items.stem: A 6 m high tree cast a 4 m long shadow. At the same time, a flag pole cast a shadow 50 m long. How long is the flag pole?
items.answer: The sun's elevation is the same for both, so triangle ABC ~ triangle PQR and AB/BC = PQ/QR. Then 6/4 = PQ/50, giving PQ = 50 × 6 ÷ 4 = 75 m. The flag pole is 75 m long.

items.stem: From the top of a 7 m high building the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°, then the height of the tower is
items.answer: Let AB = 7 m be the building and CD the tower, with BE ⊥ CD so that CE = AB = 7 m. The depression of the foot gives ∠ACB = ∠CBE = 45°, and cot45° = AC/AB in triangle ACB gives AC = 7 m, hence BE = AC = 7 m. In triangle EBD with ∠EBD = 60°, tan60° = DE/BE gives DE = 7√3 m. The tower is CE + DE = 7 + 7√3 = 7(√3 + 1) = 7 × 2.732 = 19.124 m.

items.stem: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from the points P and Q at distance of a and b respectively from the base and in the same straight line with it, are complementary. The height of the tower is
items.answer: Let the tower be AB = h and let the two points lie at distances a and b from its base. If the elevation from one is θ, the other is 90° − θ, so tanθ = h/a and tan(90° − θ) = cotθ = h/b. Multiplying, tanθ × cotθ = h²/(ab), so 1 = h²/(ab) and h = √(ab).

items.stem: From a point on the ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and the top of a transmission tower fixed at the top of a 20 m high building are 45° and 60° respectively, then the height of the tower is
items.answer: Let BC = 20 m be the building, CD = x the tower and A the point at distance y from the foot. The 45° elevation of the building's top gives tan45° = BC/AB, so 20/y = 1 and AB = y = 20 m. The 60° elevation of the tower's top gives tan60° = BD/AB, so (20 + x)/20 = √3 and 20 + x = 20√3. Hence x = 20√3 − 20 = 20 × 0.732 = 14.64 m.

Assertion : In the figure, if BC = 20 m, then height AB is 11.56 m.
Reason : tanθ = AB/BC = perpendicular/base where θ is the angle ∠ACB.
items.assertion: In the figure, if BC = 20 m, then height AB is 11.56 m.
items.reason: tanθ = AB/BC = perpendicular/base where θ is the angle ∠ACB.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: In the figure the right angle is at B and ∠ACB = 30°, so tan30° = AB/BC = AB/20. Then AB = 20/√3 = 20/1.73 = 11.56 m, and the assertion is true. The reason states exactly the ratio used, tanθ = perpendicular/base for θ = ∠ACB, so it is true and is the correct explanation of the assertion. Thus (a) is the correct option.
